473	        "collapsed": false
474	      },
475	      "rollDice": {
476	        "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
477	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
478	        "collapsed": false
479	      },
480	      "end": {
481	        "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
482	        "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
483	        "collapsed": false
484	      }
485	    }
486	  }
487	}
488	```
489	
490	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
491	
492	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
493	
494	```bash
495	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
496	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
497	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json
498	```
499	
500	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.
501	
502	> **Never write definitions by hand.** The registry is the authoritative source; hand-written definitions will fail validation or cause runtime errors.
503	
504	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
505	
506	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). Preserve its lifecycle-generated contents; project scaffolding creates it, and the Flow lifecycle regenerates it before execution or publication.
507	
508	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
509	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
510	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
511	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
512	
513	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
514	
515	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
516	
517	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
518	
519	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
520	
521	```json
522	"bindings": [
523	  {
524	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
525	    "name": "name",
526	    "type": "string",
527	    "resource": "process",
528	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
529	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
530	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
531	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
532	  },
533	  {
534	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
535	    "name": "folderPath",
536	    "type": "string",
537	    "resource": "process",
538	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
539	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
540	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
541	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
542	  }
543	]
544	```
545	
546	**Rules:**
547	
548	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
549	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
550	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
551	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
552	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
553	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
554	
555	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
556	
557	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_bindings.py <flow>` reads each resource node's definition (`model.bindings.resourceKey` / `resourceSubType` and the `<bindings.NAME>` placeholders in `model.context[]`) and reports every missing `(resourceKey, name)` entry, plus duplicates and unused entries. `--emit` prints the missing entries as JSON; `--apply` appends them to the flow and refuses when the definition does not supply `resource` / `resourceSubType` — in that case take the exact shape from the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
558	
559	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
560	
561	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
562	
563	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
564	
565	## Bindings — connector connection binding
566	
567	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
568	
569	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.
570

It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. 3	Strategy selection and shared concepts for modifying `.flow` files. Direct `.flow` authoring is required for non-carve-out structural edits; CLI is reserved for the documented product-managed configuration carve-outs.

5	## Tool Selection Ladder
6	
7	> **Pick the lowest-numbered tool that fits the operation.** If no rung fits, stop and ask the user. Scripting languages (`python`, `node`, `jq`, `sed`, `awk`, shell heredocs) are a last resort and require explicit user approval — see rung 4.
8	>
9	> 1. **CLI-managed carve-outs only** → use the relevant plugin workflow for connector activity, connector-trigger, or managed HTTP operations when the CLI populates product-managed state (`inputs.detail`, `bindings_v2.json`, connection resources).
10	> 2. **Any structural `.flow` mutation** (add/delete OOTB nodes, add/delete edges, add/edit variables, in-place value tweaks, output mapping, subflows, scheduled triggers, non-connector resources, inline-agent node/wiring) → `Edit`.
11	> 3. **Wholesale file rewrite** (only when ≥70% of nodes change, e.g., scaffolding from a template) → `Write` — but never on a flow that already contains CLI-owned nodes (connector, connector-trigger, managed HTTP): the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` and `flow validate` won't catch it. Use `Edit` (rung 2); if you do `Write`, re-run `node configure` **as the last write** to touch `inputs.detail` / `bindings[]` (a later `Write` re-clobbers it). See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
12	> 3b. **The skill's own scripts** (`scripts/flow_edit.py`, `scripts/flow_compose.py`) → the documented recipes below, applied by parsing the JSON instead of matching text. Use them for the mutations they cover, especially when one operation touches several top-level arrays; they enforce this file's rules (both ports, id patterns, definition/variable/layout upkeep, delete cascade) and refuse CLI-owned node types. They are part of this skill, not the ad-hoc scripting in rung 4 — but they still hide the line-by-line diff `Edit` shows, so prefer `Edit` for a single reviewable value change, and read the script before trusting it with an unfamiliar shape.
13	> 4. **Anything else** → STOP and ask the user. A scripting language is a last resort: surface the trade-offs (state bypass, opaque diff, no interruption point) and present finite options — typically **Use `Edit` instead** / **Use `Write` (full rewrite)** / **Approve the script for this change** / **Cancel** / **Something else**. Only proceed after the user explicitly approves that path for this specific change. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md).
14	
15	### Why not Python / Node / jq / sed?
16	
17	- The CLI auto-manages cross-cutting state (`definitions[]`, `variables.nodes`, edge references, layout). A scripting mutation bypasses that and forces hand-rolling it — extra surface for mistakes.
18	- `Edit` shows a line-by-line diff in the transcript; a script is an opaque payload. The user reviews tool calls, not script bodies.
19	- `Edit` calls are atomic per-call. A coordinated multi-section change is *not* one transaction — it's a sequence of `Edit` calls the user can interrupt between. Treating it as a single Python script removes that interruption point.
20	
21	Those trade-offs are why ad-hoc scripting is approval-gated. `scripts/flow_edit.py` / `scripts/flow_compose.py` answer the first point (they maintain `definitions[]`, `variables.nodes`, edge references and layout entries themselves) and print what they changed per call, but they still replace a reviewable diff with a summary line.
22	
23	If the change feels too tangled for a sequence of `Edit` calls, use `Write` for the whole file or stop and ask the user (see rung 4 above) — see the `Edit`/`Write` recipes in [editing-operations-json.md](editing-operations-json.md) and the SKILL.md rule on forbidden tools.

69	## Shared Rules
70	
71	These apply regardless of which strategy you use.
72	
73	### Definitions
74	
75	- Every unique `type:typeVersion` pair in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`
76	- Definitions come from `uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json` — copy the returned node definition object (`Data.Node` or the top-level node object, depending on CLI/plugin version)
77	- **Never hand-write definitions** — hand-written definitions cause validation failures
78	- One definition per unique type, not one per node instance
79	
80	### Layout
81	
82	- Layout (`layout.nodes`, `subflows[<id>].layout`) is owned by `uip maestro flow format` — do not hand-compute coordinates
83	- When authoring a node, any placeholder `position` is fine (e.g. `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`); format rewrites it on save
84	- Run `uip maestro flow format <file>.flow` after edits and before publish/debug — see [cli-commands.md](../../shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)
85	
86	### Edge rules
87	
88	- `targetPort` is required on every edge — validate rejects edges without it
89	- See [file-format.md — Standard ports](../../shared/file-format.md) for port names by node type
90	- Dynamic ports: decision (`true`/`false`), switch (`case-{id}`/`default`), HTTP (`branch-{id}`/`default`), loop (`output`/`success`/`loopBack`)
91	
92	### Validation
93	
94	- Run `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py <ProjectName>.flow` after all edits complete — it reports the structural defects `validate` does not catch (topology, `=js:` fields, Jint constructs, resource bindings, runtime gaps)
95	- Run `uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json` **once** after all edits complete
96	- Do not validate after each individual edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid
97	- Validation checks: JSON schema, definitions coverage, edge references, unique IDs
98	- Validation does NOT check: connector configuration, connection health, expression correctness, required field completeness
99	
100	### Parallel same-file Edits
101	
102	Applies to any turn that issues more than one `Edit` against the same `.flow` (greenfield T2 and brownfield alike):
103	
104	- **Same-file Edits serialize in execution order** — they do not race, but each later Edit runs against the text the earlier ones already changed. An `old_string` that overlaps text a prior Edit removed or shifted fails with "string not found."
105	- **Anchor each Edit on its target array's OWN opening key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`), located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." Top-level key order and presence are not guaranteed (see [file-format.md](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure)).
106	- **`"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique** — they recur inside inline `definitions[]` and inside any `subflows.<id>` block. Anchor on the 2-space-indented (top-level) occurrence and extend until the match is unique.
107	- Insert at the array's head (right after `[`) so the `old_string` never spans the array's closing `]`.
108	
109	Full per-array anchor table and worked example: [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
110	
111	### Expression prefix rules
112	
113	- Use `=js:` on **value expressions**: end node output `source`, variable updates, HTTP input fields, node `inputs` values
114	- Do NOT use `=js:` on **condition expressions**: decision `expression`, switch case `expression`, HTTP branch `conditionExpression` — these are always evaluated as JS automatically
115	
116	See [variables-and-expressions.md](../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for the full expression reference.
